_comment: All company names, contacts, and scenario details in this file are illustrative composites — not real customer engagements.

evals.prompt: Write the demo script for Meridian Financial. Alex Rivera will be our only contact in the meeting — Sam Chen won't be there. Keep it focused on what Alex can take back to his leadership.
evals.expected_output: meridian-financial-demo-script.md shaped for champion_enablement (single contact, no DM present), 25-35 min runtime, closes with 'what to show Sam' framing. meridian-financial-demo-brief.md for AE. No competitor mentions. Uses customer's verbatim language.
assertions: Script runtime is 25-35 min (champion enablement, not a full technical deep-dive)
Human story centers on the champion's role and the internal problem they're trying to solve
Close positions the demo as something the champion can show the DM — internal ammunition framing
No mention of competitors in scene talking points (context/do-not-mention sections may name them for SE awareness)
Uses verbatim language from discovery notes
Does not use internal sales terms (champion, deal stage, ICP)
Demo brief is one page and written for the AE, not the SE

evals.prompt: Generate the demo script for Nortech Telecom SOC-T. Audience is a mixed SOC team. We want to cover ML anomaly detection, ES|QL threat hunting, and AI Assistant — ELSER needs setup first.
evals.expected_output: nortech-telecom-demo-script.md with 3 scenes, ML first (earn trust), ES|QL second, AI Assistant third with setup caveat. Human story is a SOC analyst. Exec bridge at each transition. Platform note for ELSER setup requirement.
assertions: ML anomaly detection is Scene 1 (earn trust — they already use it)
AI Assistant scene includes explicit pre-demo setup note for LLM connector
Human story is a SOC analyst, not a generic 'user'
Exec bridge present at each scene transition
Platform notes section references the amber audit status and pre-demo task list
No scenes scripted for Agent Builder or Workflows (upgrade_required)

evals.prompt: Write the demo script for the TechSci Analytics call with the technical lead. Thursday is the deadline — keep it tight.
evals.expected_output: techsci-analytics-demo-script.md with urgency reflected, RAG demo focus, decision maker in the room, specific scenario referencing historical project data. Brief for AE.
assertions: Script reflects Thursday deadline urgency — tight runtime, no padding
Demo scenario references historical project data or institutional memory pain point
Decision maker addressed in audience section
RAG or semantic search is the primary feature scene
Confirmation doc language does not use internal sales terms
Next steps section asks for specific data or access needed for POC

evals.prompt: Write the demo script for Apex Cloud. An opportunity-profile.json is available with two quantified success goals: 'MTTR under 15 minutes' and 'false positive rate below 3%'. The value confirmation close should reference these explicitly.
evals.expected_output: apex-cloud-demo-script.md whose Scene 3 close explicitly references both success goals by name and measure. The technical win statement names 'MTTR < 15 min' and '< 3% false positive rate' rather than generic criteria.
assertions: opportunity-profile.json is read and opportunity_overview.success_goals is consumed
Value confirmation close in the final scene explicitly names each success goal
At least one quantified measure (e.g. '15 minutes', '3%') appears in the close scene talking points
Close does NOT use generic criteria from demo-goals.md when opportunity profile is present
If a goal measure is '⚠️ Not quantified', close uses directional language instead
